drugRefs.dose: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h + Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
drugRefs.why: This combination covers the major contiguous-spread pathogens (streptococci, anaerobes, and many Enterobacteriaceae) and provides good CNS penetration, appropriate pending culture/aspirate results.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Add Vancomycin if S. aureus risk (post-neurosurgery, hematogenous spread, endocarditis)
drugRefs.why: Added for empiric MRSA/staphylococcal coverage specifically when the clinical context suggests hematogenous or post-surgical seeding.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Meropenem (broader gram-negative coverage, e.g. otogenic source with Pseudomonas risk)
drugRefs.coverage: Broader alternative when gram-negative coverage including Pseudomonas is specifically needed (e.g., chronic otitis/mastoiditis as the source).

coverageMatrix.completeness: Combination covers the major contiguous-spread pathogens; staphylococcal coverage must be added based on specific risk factors.
gaps: Pseudomonas and other resistant gram-negatives not reliably covered - add broader coverage if otogenic/post-surgical source with relevant risk factors.

stewardship.deescalation: Once aspirate culture identifies the organism(s), narrow to the most targeted regimen; continue for the full 6-8 week course with serial imaging to confirm resolution before considering early discontinuation.

framework: Antibiotics alone are frequently insufficient - neurosurgical aspiration/drainage is both diagnostic (culture) and therapeutic for abscesses of sufficient size, and should not be delayed in favor of antibiotics alone.
De-escalate aggressively once aspirate culture results are available - empiric triple/broad coverage is a starting point, not the intended endpoint.
Total duration (6-8 weeks) is substantially longer than most CNS infections - do not apply standard meningitis duration logic here.
